summary: SSID name collision between wired-profile and 5GHz SSID causes dock attach to flip interface priority; VPN client fails to auto-start and DNS suffix removed
description:
Issue summary:
When a user connects their company laptop to a Dell Thunderbolt dock in the SF office while the dock uplink is on a 5GHz SSID that shares a name similar to the wired corporate network profile, Windows flips interface priority and marks the Wi-Fi as the active network. The corporate VPN client (WireGuard-based internal helper) does not auto-start on the new active interface and the Windows DNS search suffix for the corp domain is cleared. Impacted users cannot reach internal services (git, jira, private-metrics) until manual steps are taken.

Impact:
- Intermittent loss of internal host resolution after dock attach / undock cycle for ~25 users in SF office.
- VPN not reconnecting automatically, requiring manual start of the client.
- Affects domain-joined Windows laptops on modern builds (Win10/11).

Environment:
- Platform: Domain-joined Windows 10/11 laptops
- VPN: Internal WireGuard wrapper (corp-vpn.exe) v2.3.1
- Docking hardware: Dell D6000 Thunderbolt docks (firmware 1.2.5)
- Wireless: Ruckus 5GHz SSIDs with names that partially match wired profile names (example: "Redwood-Office" vs "Redwood-Office-Wired")
- DHCP: corporate DHCP + DNS search suffix via option 15 and Option 119 in some switches

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot laptop and verify it is connected to wired Ethernet via dock (or start with Wi-Fi connected).
2) With VPN disconnected, undock and connect to office 5GHz Wi-Fi SSID that has a similar name to wired profile.
3) Re-dock while Wi-Fi remains connected. Windows may flip the active interface to the Wi-Fi adapter based on metric changes.
4) Observe that corporate VPN does not auto-start and DNS search suffix for ".redwood.corp" is missing.
5) Attempt to resolve internal hosts or access private dashboards; failures observed.

Observed behavior:
- Interface metric changes cause Windows to prefer wireless adapter.
- VPN client fails to detect network state change and does not start.
- DNS search suffix is sometimes removed (no domain suffix -> short hostnames don't resolve).

Expected behavior:
- Dock attach should preserve wired priority when a dock is present and resume VPN auto-start on network change. DNS suffix should remain intact.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- System event logs snippet (Event IDs 4201, 1001) captured from affected laptop (see logs attached in Jira).
- corp-vpn client logs: "network-change detected but no eligible adapter found" repeated.
- Wireshark capture showing DNS queries leaving to 8.8.8.8 in absence of corp DNS.

Temporary workaround:
- Manual start of corp-vpn.exe restores connectivity.
- Running `netsh interface ip set interface "Ethernet" metric=10` and `netsh interface ip set interface "Wi-Fi" metric=50` restores wired preference until next reboot.
- IT can enforce naming convention for SSIDs to avoid overlap; instruct users to avoid connecting to SSIDs that are named similarly to wired profiles.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Windows Network Location Awareness / Connection Manager flips metrics on dock attach and treats the Wi-Fi as the active network. The VPN helper relies on NLA events but filters by interface description; in this case the interface name or GUID reported changed and the helper did not match it.

What we checked:
- Reproduced on 3 devices with same dock model.
- Confirmed corp-vpn ignores new interface when GUID does not match stored mapping.
- Verified DNS suffix removal correlates with a DHCP/802.1X interaction: when Wi-Fi connects first it receives DHCP options without domain-suffix; when docking later, Windows doesn't merge suffix list.
- Looked at Group Policy: there is an existing policy that sets DNS suffix via DHCP but client behavior on interface transition is flaky.

Next steps:
- Short-term: push a configuration script via Intune to set interface metrics for docked Ethernet (sets lower metric for Ethernet, higher for Wi-Fi). Useful for known dock models.
- Medium-term: update corp-vpn helper to match by interface mac/adapter class instead of stored interface GUID and trigger an explicit reconnect on any network-change event.
- Long-term: adjust SSID naming to remove ambiguity and update DHCP option distribution to ensure DNS suffix is consistently applied to Wi-Fi; consider enforcing 802.1X profiles for employees to avoid DHCP gaps.
resolution:
In progress - temporary mitigation deployed: Intune policy (Device configuration script) rolled out to SF office Windows devices to set static interface metrics on docking events and force a restart of the corp-vpn service after docking. A follow-up task has been created to change corp-vpn's network-change handler to be more robust.

Planned permanent fixes:
- PR#4532 in internal repo to change interface matching logic in corp-vpn (targeting 2026-03-20).
- SSID nomenclature update scheduled with networking team for week of 2026-03-22.
- Confirm DHCP option distribution and ensure DNS suffix 15 is present for corporate SSIDs.
